# Support LingBot-Video MoE: image-to-video, text-to-image, refiner, and prompt rewriting ## Motivation The initial LingBot-Video MoE 30B-A3B port covered text-to-video. The released checkpoint also ships refiner weights and supports image-to-video and text-to-image, so a deployment today exercises only part of what the model can do. This PR closes that gap. Related issue: #32336 Upstream PR: #32341 ## Design One pipeline serves every task. `task_type` becomes `TI2V`, which makes the input image optional, so the request decides: `image_path` gives image-to-video, omitting it gives text-to-video, `num_frames=1` gives a still. The checkpoint leaves little choice here — `model_index.json` declares a single pipeline class and the registry resolves a single config, so a second class would be unreachable without an extra CLI flag on every image-to-video request. Conditioning uses the frame twice: as visual context for the Qwen3-VL encoder, and as a clean latent pinned to the head of the diffusion latent and rewritten after every scheduler step. The DiT forward signature is untouched. The refiner is the one part behind an explicit `--pipeline-class-name LingBotVideoRefinerPipeline`, since doubling resident DiT weights is a deployment decision rather than a per-request one. It loads from the checkpoint's `refiner/` subfolder by redirecting only the weight path, so the component keeps its `transformer_2` identity and still resolves the transformer loader. Its second pass rebuilds text conditioning without vision tokens because the refiner DiT has no image-conditioning path, drives both posterior samples and the noise draw from one seeded generator, and rejects single-frame requests. Prompt rewriting runs as a stage in two turns: a free-text prompt is expanded, then mapped to JSON. Structured captions pass through untouched. There are two ways to supply the rewriter: `rewriter_url` points at a served vision language model over an OpenAI-compatible endpoint, or `rewriter_model_path` plus `rewriter_adapter_path` loads it inside the diffusion worker. The endpoint keeps another 27B model out of the worker; the in-process path saves standing up a second server. Setting neither skips the stage. ## Verification Checked against the reference diffusers implementation on the same hardware, checkpoint, seed, and parameters. Cross-GPU comparison is not meaningful for this model — identical code and seed on an H100 and a 5090 produce visibly different motion — so every comparison below is same-hardware. ### Prompts and inputs The DiT consumes a structured JSON caption rather than a plain sentence, so the prompt below is the caption itself. > [!CAUTION]
> The consumer version of Gemini Code Assist on GitHub has been sunset. All code review activity has officially ceased.

Hey, @mickqian, this PR is ready for review now. Extends the existing T2V support so one checkpoint covers image-to-video and text-to-image, adds the refiner second pass and the prompt rewriter the model was released with, and makes the DiT sequence-parallel. ## feat **Sequence parallelism.** The DiT now shards the joint `[video; text]` sequence across ranks and gathers afterwards, so `--ulysses-degree > 1` works. It was not SP-aware before while `USPAttention` engaged its all-to-all, which produced a corrupted clip rather than an error. **Image-to-video.** Qwen3-VL encodes the condition frame as an image alongside the caption; the first latent frame is pinned to it for the whole denoising loop. **Text-to-image.** `--num-frames 1`, with frame-count alignment disabled and a still-image negative prompt. **Refiner second pass.** Decodes the base clip, upscales, re-encodes, and denoises again from `t_thresh` down on the `transformer_2` weights. **Prompt rewriter.** Turns a plain prompt into the structured JSON caption the DiT expects, in two turns against either a served endpoint or an in-process VLM. Optionally also prunes the negative prompt per request. Fixes along the way: head divisibility is now checked at startup instead of deep inside the all-to-all; latent frames are no longer rounded up to the GPU count; a Video API request with `n > 1` is split into one request per output. ## Using it Prompts are structured JSON captions, not free text — see the `recipe` for the schema. The rewriter writes them for you. Both it and the refiner are off by default. ```json { "rewriter_model_path": "Qwen/Qwen3.6-27B", "rewriter_adapter_path": "" } ``` ```bash sglang serve --model-path robbyant/lingbot-video-moe-30b-a3b \ --pipeline-class-name LingBotVideoRefinerPipeline ``` ## Output **Text-to-video** and **text-to-image**, structured caption, 832x480: https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/22dc4a51-4b6d-41b1-8e4b-9cc805176080 **Image-to-video**, condition frame pinned as the first frame: https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f450ac15-2844-474b-8f4f-339f64f48fd6 **Rewriter and refiner on the same prompt.** Plain input: `a red fox trotting through fresh snow in a pine forest at sunrise`. The rewriter expands it to a structured caption, then the same caption runs through the base pipeline and through the refiner: | | Resolution | End to end | | --- | --- | --- | | base | 832x480 | 106 s | | refiner | 1920x1088 | 597 s | https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/993eaf0f-e05f-47b9-8252-d7492c3e2128 https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/5cbbdb43-73ef-437e-b087-54820ae5ecc4 ## Benchmark 8x H100 80GB, 480x832, 121 frames, 40 steps, guidance 3.0, flow shift 3.0, seed 42, same caption and sequential CFG on both sides. | Stack | Parallelism | Denoise | Per step | End to end | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | upstream diffusers | FSDP 8 | 409 s | 10.23 s | 469 s | | SGLang | `--ulysses-degree 8` | 73 s | 1.83 s | 175 s | 5.6x faster denoise, 2.7x end to end. Sharding weights only on both sides, upstream FSDP against SGLang `--tp-size 8`, SGLang denoises the same workload in 139 s. | Task | Parallelism | Denoise | Decode | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | Text-to-image (1 frame) | `--ulysses-degree 8` | 31.8 s | 0.2 s | | Image-to-video (121 frames) | `--tp-size 8` | 134 s | 4.7 s | | Refiner, both passes | `--ulysses-degree 8` + FSDP | 57 s + 100 s | 7.5 s | Output matches the upstream reference in subject, composition, and motion without being bit-identical: PSNR 20.7 dB / SSIM 0.82 on the luma plane. Some of that gap is unavoidable here — swapping only the attention kernel inside the reference stack, with everything else fixed, already moves its own output by a similar margin, and this model amplifies small input differences over 40 steps. I have not pinned down how much of the remainder is the two stacks disagreeing versus the two GPUs disagreeing; separating those needs the same code on the same card. ## Tests 81 unit tests, covering the SP shard round-trip at degrees 2/3/4, the head divisibility guard, multi-output splitting, the refiner schedule and per-output seeding, rewriter backend selection and the two-turn adapter switch, and delete-only negative pruning. ## Update: CFG parallel and cache-dit Two more knobs work on this model now. **CFG parallel.** `--cfg-parallel-size 2` splits the conditional and unconditional passes across two ranks. This needed no model-side change — the shared denoising stage already handled it once the pipeline was wired up, so this is a report that it works rather than a code change. **cache-dit.** `--enable-cache-dit` needed one entry in the custom block adapter table: the DiT's blocks live under `blocks` and its block signature is `Pattern_3`, same shape as the MiniMax-H3 entry already there. Enabling it also turned up a bug in shared code. `DenoisingStage` passed `has_separate_cfg=batch.do_classifier_free_guidance` when setting up cache-dit, which ignores CFG parallel. Under CFG parallel each rank only ever runs one branch, so that rank never sees the conditional/unconditional alternation the flag promises, and cache-dit sat waiting for a pattern that never arrived — it skipped nothing at all. Before the fix, `--enable-cache-dit` on top of `--cfg-parallel-size 2` produced a byte-identical video to leaving it off. This affects any model combining the two flags, not just LingBot. ### Speed 2x RTX 5090 32GB, no NVLink, layerwise DiT offload on. 832x480, 161 frames (10 s at 16 fps), structured caption, seed 0, guidance 3.0. Per-stage wall clock from the server log. 8 steps, fox prompt: | Configuration | Denoise | End to end | Peak | s/step | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | 1 GPU | 171.3 s | 184.8 s | 11410 MB | 21.18 | | TP 2 | 113.1 s | 123.5 s | 11370 MB | 13.97 | | CFG parallel 2 | 86.4 s | 97.3 s | 11410 MB | 10.56 | | 1 GPU + cache-dit | 119.4 s | 133.2 s | 13310 MB | — | | CFG parallel 2 + cache-dit | 55.5 s | 66.8 s | 11410 MB | — | 40 steps, the released sampling profile, fox prompt: | Configuration | Denoise | End to end | s/step | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | CFG parallel 2 | 435.7 s | 446.4 s | 10.84 | | CFG parallel 2 + cache-dit | 171.8 s | 183.7 s | — | s/step is left out for the cache-dit rows on purpose. cache-dit does not make a step cheaper — it decides a step is close enough to the previous one and reuses the cached block residuals instead of running the blocks (`Fn=1, Bn=0`, so only the first block still runs on those steps). Dividing total denoise by the step count would mix full steps with skipped ones and read as a per-step speedup that does not exist, so the comparison here is total denoise time. CFG parallel cuts denoise 1.98x, and it also halves VAE decode because that shards with it. cache-dit cuts denoise 1.43x on this prompt at 8 steps and 2.54x at 40 steps; across fox, owl and elephant the range is 1.23x to 1.58x at 8 steps and 2.54x to 2.89x at 40. More steps leaves more neighbours similar enough to skip, and at 8 steps one skipped step is already an eighth of the trajectory. The elephant prompt gains least, which fits — its content changes fastest. Together the two reach 3.09x on denoise at 8 steps (2.57x on elephant). Sequence parallelism is slower than a single card on this box. One memory note: cache-dit costs about 1.9 GB extra on a single GPU, where it keeps a separate set of cached residuals for the conditional and unconditional passes. Under CFG parallel each rank only runs one branch, so it keeps one set and peak stays where it was. ### Output cache-dit off (left) against on (right), same prompt and seed: https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/12f89b7f-76c1-4aab-9220-572ef2c6633b

Short version of what this PR adds to LingBot-Video MoE.

1. **Image-to-video.** The condition frame goes to the Qwen3-VL encoder as an image and is
   pinned to the first latent frame for the whole denoising loop.
2. **Text-to-image.** `--num-frames 1`, with frame-count alignment off and a still-image
   negative prompt.
3. **Refiner second pass.** Decodes the base clip, upscales, re-encodes, then denoises again
   from `t_thresh` down on the `transformer_2` weights.
4. **Prompt rewriter.** Turns a plain sentence into the structured JSON caption the DiT
   expects. Either a served endpoint or an in-process VLM. Can also prune the negative
   prompt per request.
5. **Sequence parallelism.** The DiT shards the joint `[video; text]` sequence and gathers
   after, so `--ulysses-degree > 1` works. It used to produce a corrupted clip instead of
   an error.
6. **CFG parallel.** `--cfg-parallel-size 2` puts the conditional and unconditional passes
   on separate ranks. No model-side change was needed; the shared denoising stage already
   handled it. Cuts denoise 1.98x, and halves VAE decode since that shards along with it.
7. **cache-dit.** `--enable-cache-dit` needed one entry in the custom block adapter table.
   It skips steps whose output is close enough to the previous one, so it helps more at 40
   steps (2.5x to 2.9x on denoise) than at 8 (1.2x to 1.6x). Stacks with CFG parallel.
   
   
If you have some spare time, could you please help review this? Thank you so much! cc @mickqian @BBuf

# Support LingBot-Video MoE: image-to-video, text-to-image, refiner, and prompt rewriting ## Motivation The initial LingBot-Video MoE 30B-A3B port covered text-to-video. The released checkpoint also ships refiner weights and supports image-to-video and text-to-image, so a deployment today exercises only part of what the model can do. This PR closes that gap. Related issue: #32336 Upstream PR: #32341 ## Design One pipeline serves every task. `task_type` becomes `TI2V`, which makes the input image optional, so the request decides: `image_path` gives image-to-video, omitting it gives text-to-video, `num_frames=1` gives a still. The checkpoint leaves little choice here — `model_index.json` declares a single pipeline class and the registry resolves a single config, so a second class would be unreachable without an extra CLI flag on every image-to-video request. Conditioning uses the frame twice: as visual context for the Qwen3-VL encoder, and as a clean latent pinned to the head of the diffusion latent and rewritten after every scheduler step. The DiT forward signature is untouched. The refiner is the one part behind an explicit `--pipeline-class-name LingBotVideoRefinerPipeline`, since doubling resident DiT weights is a deployment decision rather than a per-request one. It loads from the checkpoint's `refiner/` subfolder by redirecting only the weight path, so the component keeps its `transformer_2` identity and still resolves the transformer loader. Its second pass rebuilds text conditioning without vision tokens because the refiner DiT has no image-conditioning path, drives both posterior samples and the noise draw from one seeded generator, and rejects single-frame requests. Prompt rewriting runs as a stage in two turns: a free-text prompt is expanded, then mapped to JSON. Structured captions pass through untouched. There are two ways to supply the rewriter: `rewriter_url` points at a served vision language model over an OpenAI-compatible endpoint, or `rewriter_model_path` plus `rewriter_adapter_path` loads it inside the diffusion worker. The endpoint keeps another 27B model out of the worker; the in-process path saves standing up a second server. +_ROOT = "universal_negative"
+
+
+def _hint_pattern(*hints: str) -> re.Pattern:
+    # Whole words only, so "knight" does not read as "night".
+    alternatives = "|".join(re.escape(hint) for hint in hints)
+    return re.compile(rf"(?<![a-z0-9])(?:{alternatives})(?![a-z0-9])")
+
+
+# Whole-category removal needs the caption to ask for it outright.
+_BLOCK_HINTS = {
+    "physical_plausibility": _hint_pattern(
+        "fantasy",
+        "surreal",
+        "dreamlike",
+        "dream-like",
+        "magic",
+        "magical",
+        "supernatural",
+        "physics-bending",
+        "physics bending",
+        "impossible physics",
+        "anti-gravity",
+        "antigravity",
+        "zero gravity",
+        "zero-gravity",
+        "weightless",
+        "weightlessness",
+        "floating in space",
+        "outer space",
+        "astronaut",
+    ),
+    "artistic_style": _hint_pattern(
+        "painting",
+        "illustration",
+        "cartoon",
+        "drawing",
+        "sketch",
+        "cgi",
+        "3d render",
+        "3d-render",
+        "digital art",
+        "anime",
+        "stylized animation",
+        "claymation",
+        "stop motion",
+        "stop-motion",
+    ),
+}
+
+# Terms the model tends to leave in even when the caption clearly asks for them.
+_FORCED_DELETIONS = (
+    (
+        _hint_pattern(
+            "dark",
+            "dim",
+            "dimly",
+            "low light",
+            "low-light",
+            "night",
+            "nighttime",
+            "moody",
+            "gloomy",
+            "ominous",
+            "deep shadow",
+            "deep shadows",
+            "dark shadows",
+        ),
+        ("underexposed", "subject hidden in darkness", "crushed blacks"),

+    (

+            "motion-blur",
+            "blurred background",
+            "blurred landscape",
+            "blurred scenery",
+            "blurred surroundings",
+            "speed blur",
+            "long exposure",
+        ),
+        ("motion blur",),
+    ),

+
+def categorized_negative(negative_prompt: str) -> dict | None:
+    # A request may send any negative, so the shipped schema is checked before indexing.
+    parsed = parse_caption(negative_prompt)
+    if not isinstance(parsed, dict):
+        return None
+    categories = parsed.get(_ROOT)
+    if not isinstance(categories, dict):
+        return None
+    for terms in categories.values():
+        if not isinstance(terms, list):
+            return None
+        if not all(isinstance(term, str) for term in terms):
+            return None
+    return {_ROOT: categories}
+
+
+def build_prune_prompt(caption: str, mode: str, default: dict) -> str:
+    return (
+        f"{NEGATIVE_PRUNE}\n\n## MODE: {mode}\n\n"
+        f"## INTENDED CONTENT (structured caption):\n```json\n{caption}\n```\n\n"
+        "## DEFAULT NEGATIVE (delete the contradicting terms, keep the rest):\n"
+        f"```json\n{json.dumps(default, ensure_ascii=False)}\n```\n\n"
+        "Output ONLY the edited negative JSON now."
+    )
+
+
+def prune_negative(default: dict, pruned: dict | None, caption: str) -> dict:
+    """Keep the default's terms and order, dropping only what the model deleted."""

+    kept = pruned.get(_ROOT) if isinstance(pruned, dict) else None
+    lowered = caption.lower()
+    out = {}
+    for category, terms in default[_ROOT].items():
+        survivors = kept.get(category) if isinstance(kept, dict) else None
+        if not isinstance(survivors, list):
+            out[category] = list(terms)
+            continue
+        survivor_set = set(survivors)
+        out[category] = [term for term in terms if term in survivor_set]
+        hints = _BLOCK_HINTS.get(category)
+        if not out[category] and hints is not None and not hints.search(lowered):
+            out[category] = list(terms)
+    for hints, deletions in _FORCED_DELETIONS:
+        if not hints.search(lowered):
+            continue
+        for category, terms in out.items():
+            out[category] = [term for term in terms if term not in deletions]
+    return {_ROOT: out}

+
+class LingBotVideoAutoNegativeStage(PipelineStage):

+
+    The shipped negative is deliberately over-complete and self-contradictory, so
+    terms the caption legitimately wants push the sample away from the request.
+    """

+    def __init__(self, backend):
+        super().__init__()
+        self.backend = backend

+    @property

+    def forward(self, batch: Req, server_args: ServerArgs) -> Req:

+        # so the prompt is one caption and the negative it prunes belongs to it.

+            image=image,
+            use_lora=False,
+        )
+        negative = prune_negative(
+            default=default, pruned=parse_caption(raw), caption=caption
+        )
+        batch.negative_prompt = json.dumps(
+            negative, ensure_ascii=False, separators=(",", ":")
+        )
+        return batch

+IMAGE_MAX_TOKEN_NUM = 16384

+VLM_PATCH_FACTOR = 32

+def _round_by_factor(number: float, factor: int) -> int:
+    return round(number / factor) * factor
+
+
+def _ceil_by_factor(number: float, factor: int) -> int:
+    return math.ceil(number / factor) * factor
+
+
+def _floor_by_factor(number: float, factor: int) -> int:
+    return math.floor(number / factor) * factor
+
+
+def smart_resize(
+    height: int,
+    width: int,
+    factor: int,
+    min_pixels: int | None = None,
+    max_pixels: int | None = None,
+) -> tuple[int, int]:
+    if max_pixels is None:
+        max_pixels = IMAGE_MAX_TOKEN_NUM * factor**2
+    if min_pixels is None:
+        min_pixels = IMAGE_MIN_TOKEN_NUM * factor**2
+    if max_pixels < min_pixels:
+        raise ValueError("max_pixels must be greater than or equal to min_pixels.")
+    if max(height, width) / min(height, width) > MAX_RATIO:
+        raise ValueError(f"absolute aspect ratio must be smaller than {MAX_RATIO}.")
+
+    resized_height = max(factor, _round_by_factor(height, factor))
+    resized_width = max(factor, _round_by_factor(width, factor))
+    if resized_height * resized_width > max_pixels:
+        beta = math.sqrt((height * width) / max_pixels)
+        resized_height = _floor_by_factor(height / beta, factor)
+        resized_width = _floor_by_factor(width / beta, factor)
+    elif resized_height * resized_width < min_pixels:
+        beta = math.sqrt(min_pixels / (height * width))
+        resized_height = _ceil_by_factor(height * beta, factor)
+        resized_width = _ceil_by_factor(width * beta, factor)
+    return resized_height, resized_width
+
+
+def preprocess_condition_image(
+    image: PIL.Image.Image, height: int, width: int
+) -> torch.Tensor:
+    """Cover-resize then center-crop the condition frame to a 1, 3, 1, H, W tensor in 0..1."""
+
+    raw = (
+        torch.from_numpy(np.array(image.convert("RGB")))
+        .permute(2, 0, 1)
+        .unsqueeze(0)
+        .contiguous()
+    )
+    old_h, old_w = raw.shape[-2:]
+    scale = max(height / old_h, width / old_w)
+    new_h = max(math.ceil(old_h * scale), height)
+    new_w = max(math.ceil(old_w * scale), width)
+    # Resize in uint8, matching the reference implementation.
+    resized = F.interpolate(
+        raw, size=(new_h, new_w), mode="bilinear", align_corners=False
+    )
+    top = int(round((new_h - height) / 2.0))
+    left = int(round((new_w - width) / 2.0))
+    cropped = resized[:, :, top : top + height, left : left + width] / 255.0
+    return cropped.unsqueeze(2)
+

+def pixel_to_vlm_image(
+    pixel: torch.Tensor, factor: int = VLM_PATCH_FACTOR
+) -> PIL.Image.Image:
+    """Patch-aligned PIL view of the condition frame for Qwen3-VL."""
+
+    frame = pixel[0, :, 0].detach().cpu().clamp(0, 1)
+    array = frame.permute(1, 2, 0).mul(255).byte().numpy()
+    image = PIL.Image.fromarray(array, mode="RGB")
+    resized_height, resized_width = smart_resize(
+        image.height, image.width, factor=factor
+    )
+    return image.resize((resized_width, resized_height))
+

+def apply_first_frame_prefix(
+    latents: torch.Tensor, cond_latent: torch.Tensor
+) -> torch.Tensor:
+    """Returns a new tensor; inference latents cannot be updated in place."""
+
+    cond_frames = cond_latent.shape[2]
+    return torch.cat(
+        [cond_latent.to(latents.dtype), latents[:, :, cond_frames:]], dim=2
+    )

+def validate_refiner_sigmas(
+    sigmas: np.ndarray, t_thresh: float | None = None
+) -> np.ndarray:
+    arr = np.asarray(list(sigmas), dtype=np.float64)
+    if arr.ndim != 1 or arr.size == 0:
+        raise ValueError("refiner sigma schedule must be a non-empty 1D list")
+    if not np.all(np.isfinite(arr)):
+        raise ValueError("refiner sigma schedule contains non-finite values")
+    if np.any(arr < 0.0) or np.any(arr > 1.0):
+        raise ValueError(
+            f"refiner sigma schedule values must be in [0, 1], got {arr.tolist()}"
+        )
+    if arr.size > 1 and not np.all(np.diff(arr) < 0.0):
+        raise ValueError(
+            f"refiner sigma schedule must be strictly descending, got {arr.tolist()}"
+        )
+    if t_thresh is not None and abs(float(arr[0]) - float(t_thresh)) > 1e-6:
+        raise ValueError(
+            f"refiner sigma schedule must start at t_thresh={float(t_thresh)}, "
+            f"got {float(arr[0])}"
+        )
+    return arr
+
+
+def compute_refiner_sigmas(
+    *,
+    sigma_max: float,
+    sigma_min: float,
+    num_inference_steps: int,
+    shift: float,
+    t_thresh: float,
+    tail_steps: int = 0,
+) -> np.ndarray:
+    """Sigma schedule starting at t_thresh, with the flow shift already applied."""
+
+    if not 0.0 < float(t_thresh) <= 1.0:
+        raise ValueError(f"refiner t_thresh must lie in (0, 1], got {t_thresh}")
+    steps = int(num_inference_steps)
+    if steps < 1:
+        raise ValueError(f"num_inference_steps must be >= 1, got {steps}")
+    tail = int(tail_steps)
+    if tail < 0:
+        raise ValueError(f"refiner_sigma_tail_steps must be >= 0, got {tail}")
+
+    t_value = float(t_thresh)
+    base = np.linspace(float(sigma_max), float(sigma_min), steps + 1).copy()[:-1]
+    shifted = shift * base / (1.0 + (shift - 1.0) * base)
+    eps = 1e-6
+    sigmas = shifted[shifted <= t_value + eps]
+    if sigmas.size == 0 or abs(float(sigmas[0]) - t_value) > eps:
+        sigmas = np.concatenate([[t_value], sigmas])
+    if tail > 0:
+        start = float(sigmas[-1])
+        stop = min(float(sigma_min), start)
+        extra = np.linspace(start, stop, tail + 2, dtype=np.float64)[1:-1]
+        sigmas = np.concatenate([sigmas, extra])
+    return validate_refiner_sigmas(sigmas, t_value).astype(np.float32)
+
+
+def prepare_refiner_latent(
+    upscaled: torch.Tensor, noise: torch.Tensor, t_thresh: float
+) -> torch.Tensor:
+    return (1.0 - t_thresh) * upscaled + t_thresh * noise
+
+
+def resize_video_pixels(pixels: torch.Tensor, height: int, width: int) -> torch.Tensor:
+    """Bicubic resize of a B, C, T, H, W clip in 0..1."""
+
+    batch, channels, frames = pixels.shape[:3]
+    flat = pixels.transpose(1, 2).reshape(batch * frames, channels, *pixels.shape[3:])
+    resized = torch.nn.functional.interpolate(
+        flat.float(), size=(height, width), mode="bicubic", align_corners=False
+    ).clamp(0.0, 1.0)
+    return resized.reshape(batch, frames, channels, height, width).transpose(1, 2)

+    IMAGE_STEP1_EXPAND,
+    IMAGE_STEP2_MAP,
+    VIDEO_DURATION_EN,
+    VIDEO_DURATION_ZH,
+    VIDEO_STEP1_EXPAND,
+    VIDEO_STEP2_MAP,
+)

+
+_CJK = re.compile(r"[　-〿㐀-䶿一-鿿＀-￯]")
+_FENCED_JSON = re.compile(r"```(?:json)?\s*(\{.*\})\s*```", re.DOTALL)
+
+
+def build_expand_prompt(mode: str, prompt: str, duration: int) -> str:
+    if mode == "t2i":
+        return f"{IMAGE_STEP1_EXPAND}\n\nUser image prompt:\n{prompt}"
+    template = VIDEO_DURATION_ZH if _CJK.search(prompt) else VIDEO_DURATION_EN
+    duration_line = template.format(duration=duration)
+    return f"{VIDEO_STEP1_EXPAND}\n\n{prompt}\n\n{duration_line}"
+
+
+def build_map_prompt(mode: str, detailed: str, duration: int) -> str:
+    if mode == "t2i":
+        return f"{IMAGE_STEP2_MAP}\n\nDETAILED CAPTION:\n{detailed}"
+    return (
+        f"{VIDEO_STEP2_MAP}\n\nVideo Duration: {duration} seconds\n\n"
+        f"DETAILED CAPTION:\n{detailed}\n\nOutput the JSON now."
+    )
+
+
+def parse_caption(raw: str) -> dict | None:
+    """Read the mapping stage output, tolerating code fences and stray text."""
+
+    text = (raw or "").strip()
+    fenced = _FENCED_JSON.search(text)
+    if fenced:
+        text = fenced.group(1)
+    start, end = text.find("{"), text.rfind("}")
+    if start < 0 or end <= start:
+        return None
+    try:
+        caption = json.loads(text[start : end + 1])
+    except json.JSONDecodeError:
+        return None
+    return caption if isinstance(caption, dict) else None
+
+
+def resolve_mode(batch: Req) -> str:
+    if int(batch.num_frames) == 1:
+        return "t2i"
+    return "ti2v" if batch.image_path else "t2v"
+
+
+def needs_rewrite(prompt: str) -> bool:
+    """A structured caption is already in distribution, so leave it alone."""
+
+    return not prompt.lstrip().startswith("{")
+
+
+def condition_image(batch: Req) -> PIL.Image.Image:
+    """The condition frame as a PIL image, loading it if the stage runs first."""
+
+    image = batch.condition_image
+    if isinstance(image, list):
+        image = image[0]
+    if not isinstance(image, PIL.Image.Image):
+        image = load_image(batch.image_path)
+    return image.convert("RGB")
+
+
+class LingBotVideoPromptRewriteStage(PipelineStage):
+    """Expand a plain prompt into the structured caption the DiT was trained on.
+
+    Two turns against the rewriter backend: expand without the rewriter adapter,
+    then map that expansion to JSON with the adapter enabled.
+    """
+
+    def __init__(self, backend):
+        super().__init__()
+        self.backend = backend
+
+    @property
+    def parallelism_type(self) -> StageParallelismType:
+        # Rank 0 rewrites and broadcasts, so every rank denoises the same caption.
+        return StageParallelismType.MAIN_RANK_ONLY_AND_SEND_TO_OTHERS
+
+    def forward(self, batch: Req, server_args: ServerArgs) -> Req:
+        # Dynamic batching merges compatible text requests into a prompt list.
+        batched = isinstance(batch.prompt, list)
+        prompts = batch.prompt if batched else [batch.prompt]
+
+        mode = resolve_mode(batch)
+        duration = max(1, round(int(batch.num_frames) / max(int(batch.fps), 1)))
+        image = condition_image(batch) if mode == "ti2v" else None
+        rewritten = [self._rewrite(p, mode, duration, image) for p in prompts]
+
+        batch.prompt = rewritten if batched else rewritten[0]
+        return batch
+
+    def _rewrite(
+        self, prompt: str, mode: str, duration: int, image: PIL.Image.Image | None
+    ) -> str:
+        if not needs_rewrite(prompt):
+            return prompt
+        detailed = self.backend.generate(
+            build_expand_prompt(mode, prompt, duration), image, use_lora=False
+        )
+        raw = self.backend.generate(
+            build_map_prompt(mode, detailed, duration), image, use_lora=True
+        )
+        caption = parse_caption(raw)
+        if caption is None:
+            # Falling back to the plain prompt would denoise out of distribution
+            # and emit a broken video rather than fail.
+            raise ValueError(
+                "Prompt rewriting produced no parseable structured caption. "
+                "Pass a structured JSON caption directly, or check the rewriter backend."
+            )
+        return json.dumps(caption, ensure_ascii=False, separators=(",", ":"))

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0

+import base64
+import io
+
+import PIL.Image
+import requests
+
+from sglang.multimodal_gen.runtime.utils.logging_utils import init_logger
+
+logger = init_logger(__name__)
+
+
+class HTTPRewriterBackend:
+    """Call an OpenAI-compatible endpoint, selecting a model per turn."""
+
+    def __init__(
+        self,
+        url: str,
+        map_url: str,
+        expand_model: str,
+        map_model: str,
+        timeout: float,
+    ):
+        self.url = url.rstrip("/")
+        self.map_url = map_url.rstrip("/")
+        self.expand_model = expand_model
+        self.map_model = map_model
+        self.timeout = timeout
+
+    def generate(self, text: str, image: PIL.Image.Image | None, use_lora: bool) -> str:
+        content: list[dict] = [{"type": "text", "text": text}]
+        if image is not None:
+            content.insert(
+                0, {"type": "image_url", "image_url": {"url": _data_url(image)}}
+            )
+        response = requests.post(
+            f"{self.map_url if use_lora else self.url}/v1/chat/completions",
+            json={
+                "model": self.map_model if use_lora else self.expand_model,
+                "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": content}],
+                "temperature": 0.0,
+                # The mapping turn must answer with JSON and nothing else.
+                "chat_template_kwargs": {"enable_thinking": False},
+            },
+            timeout=self.timeout,
+        )
+        response.raise_for_status()
+        return response.json()["choices"][0]["message"]["content"].strip()
+
+
+class TransformersRewriterBackend:
+    """Base VLM plus the rewriter adapter, loaded in this process on first use.
+
+    The adapter ships a regex ``target_modules`` over the unfused Qwen3.5
+    projections, which peft applies directly and the SGLang LoRA path does not
+    accept, so serving it needs this loader or a pre-merged checkpoint.
+    """
+
+    def __init__(
+        self,
+        model_path: str,
+        adapter_path: str,
+        device_map: str,
+        max_new_tokens: int,
+    ):
+        self.model_path = model_path
+        self.adapter_path = adapter_path
+        self.device_map = device_map
+        self.max_new_tokens = max_new_tokens
+        self.processor = None
+        self.model = None
+
+    def _load(self) -> None:
+        import torch
+        from peft import PeftModel
+        from transformers import AutoModelForImageTextToText, AutoProcessor
+
+        logger.info(
+            "Loading the prompt rewriter from %s with adapter %s ...",
+            self.model_path,
+            self.adapter_path,
+        )
+        self.processor = AutoProcessor.from_pretrained(
+            self.model_path, trust_remote_code=True
+        )
+        base = AutoModelForImageTextToText.from_pretrained(
+            self.model_path,
+            torch_dtype=torch.bfloat16,
+            device_map=self.device_map,
+            trust_remote_code=True,
+        )
+        self.model = PeftModel.from_pretrained(base, self.adapter_path).eval()
+
+    def generate(self, text: str, image: PIL.Image.Image | None, use_lora: bool) -> str:
+        import contextlib
+
+        import torch
+
+        if self.model is None:
+            self._load()
+        content = [{"type": "image", "image": image}] if image is not None else []
+        content.append({"type": "text", "text": text})
+        chat = self.processor.apply_chat_template(
+            [{"role": "user", "content": content}],
+            tokenize=False,
+            add_generation_prompt=True,
+            enable_thinking=False,
+        )
+        inputs = self.processor(
+            text=[chat],
+            images=[image] if image is not None else None,
+            return_tensors="pt",
+        ).to(self.model.device)
+        adapter = contextlib.nullcontext() if use_lora else self.model.disable_adapter()
+        with torch.no_grad(), adapter:
+            out = self.model.generate(
+                **inputs, max_new_tokens=self.max_new_tokens, do_sample=False
+            )
+        generated = out[:, inputs["input_ids"].shape[1] :]
+        return self.processor.batch_decode(generated, skip_special_tokens=True)[
+            0
+        ].strip()
+
+
+def build_rewriter_backend(config):
+    if config.rewriter_url is not None:
+        return HTTPRewriterBackend(
+            url=config.rewriter_url,
+            map_url=config.rewriter_map_url or config.rewriter_url,
+            expand_model=config.rewriter_expand_model,
+            map_model=config.rewriter_map_model,
+            timeout=config.rewriter_timeout,
+        )
+    if config.rewriter_model_path is None:
+        return None
+    if config.rewriter_adapter_path is None:
+        raise ValueError(
+            "rewriter_model_path needs rewriter_adapter_path: the mapping turn is "
+            "the base VLM with the rewriter adapter enabled."
+        )
+    return TransformersRewriterBackend(
+        model_path=config.rewriter_model_path,
+        adapter_path=config.rewriter_adapter_path,
+        device_map=config.rewriter_device_map,
+        max_new_tokens=config.rewriter_max_new_tokens,
+    )
+
+
+def _data_url(image: PIL.Image.Image) -> str:
+    buffer = io.BytesIO()
+    image.convert("RGB").save(buffer, format="PNG")
+    return f"data:image/png;base64,{base64.b64encode(buffer.getvalue()).decode()}"

Hey, @mickqian, this PR is ready for review now. Extends the existing T2V support so one checkpoint covers image-to-video and text-to-image, adds the refiner second pass and the prompt rewriter the model was released with, and makes the DiT sequence-parallel. ## feat **Sequence parallelism.** The DiT now shards the joint `[video; text]` sequence across ranks and gathers afterwards, so `--ulysses-degree > 1` works. It was not SP-aware before while `USPAttention` engaged its all-to-all, which produced a corrupted clip rather than an error. **Image-to-video.** Qwen3-VL encodes the condition frame as an image alongside the caption; the first latent frame is pinned to it for the whole denoising loop. **Text-to-image.** `--num-frames 1`, with frame-count alignment disabled and a still-image negative prompt. **Refiner second pass.** Decodes the base clip, upscales, re-encodes, and denoises again from `t_thresh` down on the `transformer_2` weights. **Prompt rewriter.** Turns a plain prompt into the structured JSON caption the DiT expects, in two turns against either a served endpoint or an in-process VLM. Optionally also prunes the negative prompt per request. Fixes along the way: head divisibility is now checked at startup instead of deep inside the all-to-all; latent frames are no longer rounded up to the GPU count; a Video API request with `n > 1` is split into one request per output. ## Using it Prompts are structured JSON captions, not free text — see the `recipe` for the schema. The rewriter writes them for you. Both it and the refiner are off by default. ```json { "rewriter_model_path": "Qwen/Qwen3.6-27B", "rewriter_adapter_path": "" } ``` ```bash sglang serve --model-path robbyant/lingbot-video-moe-30b-a3b \ --pipeline-class-name LingBotVideoRefinerPipeline ``` ## Output **Text-to-video** and **text-to-image**, structured caption, 832x480: https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/22dc4a51-4b6d-41b1-8e4b-9cc805176080 **Image-to-video**, condition frame pinned as the first frame: https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f450ac15-2844-474b-8f4f-339f64f48fd6 **Rewriter and refiner on the same prompt.** Plain input: `a red fox trotting through fresh snow in a pine forest at sunrise`. The rewriter expands it to a structured caption, then the same caption runs through the base pipeline and through the refiner: | | Resolution | End to end | | --- | --- | --- | | base | 832x480 | 106 s | | refiner | 1920x1088 | 597 s | https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/993eaf0f-e05f-47b9-8252-d7492c3e2128 https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/5cbbdb43-73ef-437e-b087-54820ae5ecc4 ## Benchmark 8x H100 80GB, 480x832, 121 frames, 40 steps, guidance 3.0, flow shift 3.0, seed 42, same caption and sequential CFG on both sides. | Stack | Parallelism | Denoise | Per step | End to end | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | upstream diffusers | FSDP 8 | 409 s | 10.23 s | 469 s | | SGLang | `--ulysses-degree 8` | 73 s | 1.83 s | 175 s | 5.6x faster denoise, 2.7x end to end. Sharding weights only on both sides, upstream FSDP against SGLang `--tp-size 8`, SGLang denoises the same workload in 139 s. | Task | Parallelism | Denoise | Decode | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | Text-to-image (1 frame) | `--ulysses-degree 8` | 31.8 s | 0.2 s | | Image-to-video (121 frames) | `--tp-size 8` | 134 s | 4.7 s | | Refiner, both passes | `--ulysses-degree 8` + FSDP | 57 s + 100 s | 7.5 s | Output matches the upstream reference in subject, composition, and motion without being bit-identical: PSNR 20.7 dB / SSIM 0.82 on the luma plane. Some of that gap is unavoidable here — swapping only the attention kernel inside the reference stack, with everything else fixed, already moves its own output by a similar margin, and this model amplifies small input differences over 40 steps. I have not pinned down how much of the remainder is the two stacks disagreeing versus the two GPUs disagreeing; separating those needs the same code on the same card. ## Tests 81 unit tests, covering the SP shard round-trip at degrees 2/3/4, the head divisibility guard, multi-output splitting, the refiner schedule and per-output seeding, rewriter backend selection and the two-turn adapter switch, and delete-only negative pruning. ## Update: CFG parallel and cache-dit Two more knobs work on this model now. **CFG parallel.** `--cfg-parallel-size 2` splits the conditional and unconditional passes across two ranks. This needed no model-side change — the shared denoising stage already handled it once the pipeline was wired up, so this is a report that it works rather than a code change. **cache-dit.** `--enable-cache-dit` needed one entry in the custom block adapter table: the DiT's blocks live under `blocks` and its block signature is `Pattern_3`, same shape as the MiniMax-H3 entry already there. Enabling it also turned up a bug in shared code. `DenoisingStage` passed `has_separate_cfg=batch.do_classifier_free_guidance` when setting up cache-dit, which ignores CFG parallel. Under CFG parallel each rank only ever runs one branch, so that rank never sees the conditional/unconditional alternation the flag promises, and cache-dit sat waiting for a pattern that never arrived — it skipped nothing at all. Before the fix, `--enable-cache-dit` on top of `--cfg-parallel-size 2` produced a byte-identical video to leaving it off. This affects any model combining the two flags, not just LingBot. ### Speed 2x RTX 5090 32GB, no NVLink, layerwise DiT offload on. 832x480, 161 frames (10 s at 16 fps), structured caption, seed 0, guidance 3.0. Per-stage wall clock from the server log. 8 steps, fox prompt: | Configuration | Denoise | End to end | Peak | s/step | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | 1 GPU | 171.3 s | 184.8 s | 11410 MB | 21.18 | | TP 2 | 113.1 s | 123.5 s | 11370 MB | 13.97 | | CFG parallel 2 | 86.4 s | 97.3 s | 11410 MB | 10.56 | | 1 GPU + cache-dit | 119.4 s | 133.2 s | 13310 MB | — | | CFG parallel 2 + cache-dit | 55.5 s | 66.8 s | 11410 MB | — | 40 steps, the released sampling profile, fox prompt: | Configuration | Denoise | End to end | s/step | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | CFG parallel 2 | 435.7 s | 446.4 s | 10.84 | | CFG parallel 2 + cache-dit | 171.8 s | 183.7 s | — | s/step is left out for the cache-dit rows on purpose. cache-dit does not make a step cheaper — it decides a step is close enough to the previous one and reuses the cached block residuals instead of running the blocks (`Fn=1, Bn=0`, so only the first block still runs on those steps). Dividing total denoise by the step count would mix full steps with skipped ones and read as a per-step speedup that does not exist, so the comparison here is total denoise time. CFG parallel cuts denoise 1.98x, and it also halves VAE decode because that shards with it. cache-dit cuts denoise 1.43x on this prompt at 8 steps and 2.54x at 40 steps; across fox, owl and elephant the range is 1.23x to 1.58x at 8 steps and 2.54x to 2.89x at 40. More steps leaves more neighbours similar enough to skip, and at 8 steps one skipped step is already an eighth of the trajectory. The elephant prompt gains least, which fits — its content changes fastest. Together the two reach 3.09x on denoise at 8 steps (2.57x on elephant). Sequence parallelism is slower than a single card on this box. One memory note: cache-dit costs about 1.9 GB extra on a single GPU, where it keeps a separate set of cached residuals for the conditional and unconditional passes. Under CFG parallel each rank only runs one branch, so it keeps one set and peak stays where it was. ### Output cache-dit off (left) against on (right), same prompt and seed: https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/12f89b7f-76c1-4aab-9220-572ef2c6633b

Short version of what this PR adds to LingBot-Video MoE.

1. **Image-to-video.** The condition frame goes to the Qwen3-VL encoder as an image and is
   pinned to the first latent frame for the whole denoising loop.
2. **Text-to-image.** `--num-frames 1`, with frame-count alignment off and a still-image
   negative prompt.
3. **Refiner second pass.** Decodes the base clip, upscales, re-encodes, then denoises again
   from `t_thresh` down on the `transformer_2` weights.
4. **Prompt rewriter.** Turns a plain sentence into the structured JSON caption the DiT
   expects. Either a served endpoint or an in-process VLM. Can also prune the negative
   prompt per request.
5. **Sequence parallelism.** The DiT shards the joint `[video; text]` sequence and gathers
   after, so `--ulysses-degree > 1` works. It used to produce a corrupted clip instead of
   an error.
6. **CFG parallel.** `--cfg-parallel-size 2` puts the conditional and unconditional passes
   on separate ranks. No model-side change was needed; the shared denoising stage already
   handled it. Cuts denoise 1.98x, and halves VAE decode since that shards along with it.
7. **cache-dit.** `--enable-cache-dit` needed one entry in the custom block adapter table.
   It skips steps whose output is close enough to the previous one, so it helps more at 40
   steps (2.5x to 2.9x on denoise) than at 8 (1.2x to 1.6x). Stacks with CFG parallel.
   
   
If you have some spare time, could you please help review this? Thank you so much! cc @mickqian @BBuf
